record.original_question: Do optimal polynomial approximants have further applications in signal processing research?

evidence.quote: The use of opas in filter design doesn't seem to have gone much further in the one variable case, although some papers later in the 80s and 90s discuss related IIR filter designs. It would be interesting to know whether opas might have some further applications in signal processing research.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a Hilbert space of analytic functions on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ in which the monomials $\{z^n\}_{n\ge 0}$ form an orthogonal basis (for example, the Hardy space $H^2$, the Bergman space $A^2$, or a weighted Dirichlet-type space $D_\alpha$ with norm $\|\sum a_n z^n\|_\alpha^2 = \sum_{n\ge 0}(n+1)^\alpha |a_n|^2$). For a function $f\in\mathcal{H}$ that does not vanish identically and a nonnegative integer $n$, the optimal polynomial approximant (opa) of degree $n$ to $1/f$ in $\mathcal{H}$ is the unique polynomial $p_n$ of degree at most $n$ that minimizes
$$\|p f - 1\|_{\mathcal{H}}$$
over all polynomials $p$ of degree at most $n$. These polynomials and their reversed versions arise in connection with cyclicity in $\mathcal{H}$ and, classically, with the design of finite impulse response (FIR) and infinite impulse response (IIR) filters via least-squares inverse polynomial methods.

Problem. Identify and rigorously formulate one or more new applications of optimal polynomial approximants in signal processing — for example, in the design, analysis, or stability of FIR/IIR filters, in deconvolution, prediction, or spectral factorization problems — beyond the classical least-squares inverse FIR design of the 1970s. Specifically, exhibit a signal-processing problem (with a precise model and objective functional) whose solution is given by, or quantitatively controlled by, optimal polynomial approximants in some space $\mathcal{H}$ as above, and prove the corresponding optimality, convergence, or error-bound statement.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open-ended invitation to find further applications of optimal polynomial approximants (opas) in signal processing. A brief search shows continuing mathematical work on opas (cyclicity, zeros, Jacobi matrices) but no widely recognized new signal-processing application beyond the classical least-squares inverse FIR/IIR filter design literature, so the question remains an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Optimal polynomial approximants survey-style references
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses opas and notes that their use in filter design has not progressed substantially since the 1980s–90s, posing further applications as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: Further signal-processing applications of opas remain an open research direction.
